defined_terms.rule: A term is defined once, in bold inside brackets, without quotation marks, and used with the same capitals ever after. In a definitions clause the term is bold without quotation marks, followed by "means" or the pointer formula. Define a thing that recurs at its first mention, and only then; a term defined inside a clause also gets an entry in the definitions list pointing to it, in alphabetical order; a term defined but never used again is a slip. Defined terms are long-form, never short forms or acronyms (Memorandum of Understanding, not MoU; Liquidated Damages, not LD); industry acronyms stay (EPC, BESS).
defined_terms.pointer_formula: shall have the meaning ascribed thereto in Section [●] ([●])
source: Decisions 20 Oct 2026

placeholder.rule: Every unknown is [●] (a bracketed black circle). A neutral bracketed description is allowed where a reader needs to know what goes there: [relevant sales tax authority], [applicable PPP law]. No [•], [ ], [____] or XX.

cross_refs.rule: A reference to a provision of the same document carries its heading in brackets the first time it is made in a clause. The heading is set in italics; a reference to a sub-section (Section 7.1) carries no heading; a statutory section is cited the same way, with the Act: section 11 (Approval of Mergers) of the Competition Act, 2010.

government.rule: No government, province, provincial department or body, and no province-specific or federal-only PPP law, is named. The government party is the defined term Government, named once where it is defined in a deal's draft; departments and authorities are [●] or a neutral description in brackets. Nationwide laws and bodies stay (Companies Act, 2017; SECP; Arbitration Act, 1940; Contract Act, 1872; FBR).
source: Decisions 20 Oct 2026 (no government or province is built in)

quotations.rule: Single quotation marks only, with the quoted matter in italics; never double quotation marks. A document is referred to by its title the same way: the document entitled ‘[●]’, without page counts or a description of its format. Law reproduced word for word is introduced as ‘Section [●] of the [●] is reproduced below:’ and set in italics.
source: Usama Siddiqui's claude.ai memory, exported 2 Nov 2026 (document-standards; KPT memorandum format; Sapphire house style)

punctuation.rule: No em dashes anywhere; an en dash only inside an annexure title. No semicolon joining independent clauses: each provision is its own sentence and its own paragraph. Apostrophes are curly (’). “and/ or” takes a space after the slash. No word is broken by a hyphen at the end of a line. No contractions.
source: Usama Siddiqui's claude.ai memory, exported 2 Nov 2026 (akla-house-style; Project Cancer house style; Sapphire Volume III)

lists.rule: A list follows a lead-in ending in a colon, then items lettered (a), (b), (c), each on its own line and ending with a semicolon, “and” after the last but one; never run inline in a sentence, and never roman numerals at the first level. In a schedule or a list of points a flat 1, 2, 3 without headings. All numbering is Word’s own: never a number typed as text and pushed across with a tab, for clause numbers and (a), (i) alike.
source: Usama Siddiqui's claude.ai memory, exported 2 Nov 2026 (KPT memorandum format; Sapphire house style; document-standards)

labels.rule: A lead-in label before a colon at the start of a paragraph or cell (‘Query:’, ‘NSCL:’) is bold small caps, the colon plain. No bracketed labels such as [Inferred], [Law Silent], [Recommended] or [Firm’s View], and no risk or status ratings (Met / Not Met) in a memorandum: they read as machine-written. Nothing is written without a purpose it can justify.
source: Usama Siddiqui's claude.ai memory, exported 2 Nov 2026 (document-standards; KPT memorandum format)

names.rule: People and parties by their full names, never initials (Mr. Hashim Arshad Faruqui, not HF). The firm is Ali Khan Law Associates, never Ali Asgher Khan Law Associates; in its own correspondence it is ‘the Firm’ without a defining line (never ‘Ali Khan Law Associates (the Firm)’). The Founder’s designation is Founder; Barrister-at-Law. The other side’s law firm is never named: a defined role (the Seller’s Counsel). On a due diligence matter the DD report’s own defined terms are used, as it defines them.
source: Usama Siddiqui's claude.ai memory, exported 2 Nov 2026 (akla-house-style; M-6 standing rules; Artistic drafting standards; Sapphire house style)

tracked_changes.rule: Every tracked change is authored ‘Ali Khan Law Associates’. Only wording is tracked, never formatting, so no formatting balloons appear in the margin. Each change marks only the characters that differ: never a clause struck and retyped where the text was substantially right, and nothing struck against the counterparty’s own text beyond the change intended. Every consequential change is carried through in the same pass: cross-references, the definitions list, numbering. A comment that has been answered is deleted in that pass. Formatting, styles, margins and layout are never changed unless asked, except to match what the document already does when adding to it.
source: Usama Siddiqui's claude.ai memory, exported 2 Nov 2026 (akla-house-style; M-6 standing rules; document-standards; TSA key learnings)

layout.rule: Arial 11, justified throughout, inside tables too; A4; headings in bold small caps, Title Case with acronyms kept in capitals. Paragraph spacing before and after is 0, with one empty paragraph between clauses and none between the items of one list. In a table the Sr. No. and date columns are centred; filled-in values are not bold. ‘Page X of Y’ in the footer; ‘Privileged & Confidential’ on a client-facing document; the sign-off is ‘For And On Behalf Of’.
source: Usama Siddiqui's claude.ai memory, exported 2 Nov 2026 (akla-house-style; document-standards; M-6 standing rules; bid drafting standards)

law_currency.rule: Never cite superseded law: before an instrument is cited, check it for amendment or replacement (the Public Procurement Rules, 2026 replaced the 2004 Rules on September 28, 2026; Forms 28 and 29 were abolished by the Companies Regulations, 2024; section 15 of the NEPRA Act was replaced by section 14B in 2018). A pinpoint that cannot be verified against the primary source is removed, not kept. Nothing is stated as a consequence unless the documents expressly support it.
source: Usama Siddiqui's claude.ai memory, exported 2 Nov 2026 (M-6 standing rules; Sapphire citation corrections; IRL drafting discipline)

correspondence.rule: An email to the team opens ‘Team,’. A capitalised short form (the Bill, the Rules) is defined at first use, straight after the full title. A pleasantry sits in its own paragraph. Formal and assured, never deferential: no ‘flag’, ‘grateful’ or ‘impose’; prefer ‘inform’, ‘confirm’. In government and revenue correspondence less is more: nothing volunteered that is not required.
source: Usama Siddiqui's claude.ai memory, exported 2 Nov 2026 (M-6 standing rules; drafting-style; government correspondence principles)

file_naming.rule: A file is named <MatterCode><n> - <Document name> [<Party or author>][<Stage>][<Month DD, YYYY>], with an optional suffix after a hyphen (- Track, - Clean, - Compared, - OCR). Square brackets only, never round. A new document takes the matter’s next whole number; a document derived from another takes a decimal of its number (a markup of NSCL1 is NSCL1.1). A document the Firm circulated is tagged [AKLA][1st Cir]; internal work is tagged by its author and round ([Usama 1st WD], [Ahmed 1st Rec]). Names stay short.
examples: NSCL9.21 - GSA [AKLA][Further Changes on NSCL Draft][September 18, 2026] - Track
source: Usama Siddiqui's claude.ai memory, exported 2 Nov 2026 (file-naming; M-6 standing rules)
